issues.legal_issue: An appellate decree supersedes the trial court decree under the doctrine of merger, including where the appellate court modifies the trial court decree.

An executing court may extend the time for depositing money required by the decree where the operative appellate decree does not prescribe a time limit, without thereby impermissibly modifying the decree.

The limitation period for executing a decree is assessed in light of the appellate decree and relevant proceedings, including pending review applications, rather than solely from the date of the original trial court decree.
A transferee who acquires an interest in property during pending litigation has only limited rights under the doctrine of lis pendens and cannot use those rights to obstruct execution of the decree.
Section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act does not protect a transferee who entered into the agreement with knowledge of the pending suit from enforcement of the decree against the property.
